annotations.title: Pentecost.
annotations.text: [1] Though the Apostles might desire to come to the Iewes Festiuities, by reason of the general concourse of people to the same, the better to deale for their saluation and to spred the Gospel of Christ, yet it is like that they now kept solemly the Christian Pentecost or whitsontide, for memorie of the Holy Ghost, and that S. Paul went to that Feast of the Christians rather then the other of the Iewes. And Ven. Bede saith here, The Apostle maketh hast to keepe the fifteth day, that is, of remission and of the Holy Ghost. For, that the Christians already kept the eight day, that is, the [2] Sunday or our Lordes day, and had altered already the ordinarie Sabboth into the same, it is plaine by the Scriptures (1 Cor. 16, 2. Apoc. 1, 10.) and by antiquitie. Iustin. Mart. Apolog. 2 ad Anton. Pium in fine. And it is as like that they changed the Iewes Pasche and Pentecost as that, specially when it is euident that [3] these Festiuities be kept by Apostolike tradition, and approued by the vse of al auncient Churches and Councels.

annotations.title: Rauening wolues.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> The gouernours of the Church are foretold of the great danger that should fall to the people by wolues, that is to say, by Heretikes, whose cruelty toward the Catholikes is noted by this terme. They be knowen by the forsaking the vnitie of the Church whereof they were before, by going out and drawing many disciples after them, and by their peruerse doctrine. Such wolues came afterward in deede in diuers ages, Arius, Macedonius, Nestorius, Eutyches, Luther, Caluin, great bloudsucking wolues, and wasters of the flocke of Christ.

notes.text: Rauening wolues are the Heretikes of al ages.

annotations.title: It is a more blessed thing to giue.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> Among many other infinite goodly things and speaches which Christ spake and be not written in the Gospels, this sentence is one: which S. Paul heard of some of the Apostles daily conuersant with him, or els learned of Christ him self, or of the Holy Ghost. And it signifieth, that whereas the world commonly counteth him happie that receiueth any benefite, as almes either temporal or spiritual, <mn>[2]</mn> yet in deede he that giueth or bestoweth, is more happie. Which if the world did wel consider, men would giue almes faster then they do, if it were but for their owne benefite.

notes.text: Christs speaches not written in the Gospel.
